title.narrative: Chinese institutions and enterprises enhance OSH, labour compliance, and responsible business conduct to support decent work during green and structural transitions in China and beyond

description.narrative: China green and low carbon transition is changing employment and raising new labour, skills, and occupational safety challenges, while Chinese enterprises going global face gaps in applying international labour standards. Although green policies support decent work and just transition, climate-related risks are not yet fully integrated into its OSH governance system. The ILO has helped build enterprise capacity on labour compliance and responsible business conduct, and will continue supporting tripartite constituents to address these issues. In 2026-27, ILO interventions aim to achieve the following results: National and local stakeholders demonstrate strengthened awareness and understanding of climate related occupational safety and health risks, engage in more informed policy dialogue, and increasingly integrate climate considerations into OSH governance and prevention systems, contributing to more effective protection of workersâ€™ health in support of Chinaâ€™s climate and sustainable development objectives; Tripartite constituents and key stakeholders strengthen their capacity to understand and address employment impacts of green and structural transitions through clearer evidence and practical policy options, enabling the application of just transition principles that enhance worker protection and promote decent work. The knowledge generated also contributes to shared learning for other emerging and developing countries facing similar transitions; CEC, sectoral associations and their member companies demonstrate strengthened capacity to understand and apply the principles of international labour standards, especially the fundamental principles and rights at work, across global supply chains, leading to more systematic responsible business conducts, creation of more decent work opportunities, and contribution to the local development.
